studyOrder: Start with Cloud Concepts (24%) so the basic words, such as Region, elasticity, and pay as you go, make sense. Next study Cloud Technology and Services (34%) and Security and Compliance (30%), which together are about two-thirds of the exam. Finish with Billing, Pricing, and Support (12%), a smaller chapter that is quick to review.
hardChapters: Cloud Technology and Services is the largest chapter and has many services with similar names, so learn each one as a single sentence (for example, S3 stores objects, EBS is a disk for one EC2 instance). In Security and Compliance, many mistakes come from mixing up look-alike services such as GuardDuty, Inspector, and Macie, or CloudTrail and Config. Practice the shared responsibility model with examples until you can say right away whether a task belongs to AWS or the customer.
examDay: You have 90 minutes for 65 questions, which is a little under a minute and a half per question, so mark hard questions and come back later. Answer every question, because you cannot tell which ones are unscored. The pass mark is 700 on a scale of 100 to 1,000 for the exam as a whole, so a weaker chapter can be made up by stronger ones. Read each question for how many answers it asks for.
